module_title: Important Stadiums in India and the World - Foundational Facts
introduction: Stadiums are not just sports grounds; they are icons of a nation's sporting culture and historic milestones. In competitive exams, direct questions regarding stadiums and their locations are frequently asked under Static GK. This foundational level covers the world's and India's largest and most iconic stadiums.

core_concepts.title: World's Largest Cricket Stadium
core_concepts.description: The Narendra Modi Stadium (formerly known as Motera Stadium), located in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, is the largest cricket stadium in the world. It boasts a massive seating capacity of 1,32,000 spectators.

core_concepts.title: The Mecca of Cricket
core_concepts.description: Lord's Cricket Ground, located in London (UK), is globally revered as the 'Mecca of Cricket'. It is world-famous for its rich history, traditional ethics, and historic matches.

core_concepts.title: India's Oldest and Most Iconic Cricket Ground
core_concepts.description: Eden Gardens in Kolkata is India's oldest and one of its most prestigious cricket stadiums. Before the construction of the Narendra Modi Stadium, it held the title of the largest cricket stadium in India.

core_concepts.title: The Pride of Australia
core_concepts.description: The Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), located in Melbourne, Australia, is the second-largest cricket stadium in the world and has hosted multiple Olympic and World Cup events.

core_concepts.title: Globally Renowned Football Arena
core_concepts.description: Wembley Stadium in London (UK) is one of the most famous football stadiums globally, known for hosting major European finals, FA Cup matches, and historic FIFA World Cup fixtures.

important_entities.name: Narendra Modi Stadium
important_entities.significance: The largest cricket stadium globally with a seating capacity of 1.32 lakh.

important_entities.name: Eden Gardens
important_entities.significance: India's oldest cricket stadium, often called the 'Colosseum of Cricket'.

important_entities.name: Lord's Cricket Ground
important_entities.significance: The Mecca of Cricket; home to the MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club).

important_entities.name: Arun Jaitley Stadium
important_entities.significance: Formerly known as Feroz Shah Kotla Stadium. It is one of the historic cricket venues in northern India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants often search for 'Motera Stadium' or 'Sardar Patel Stadium' in exam options. Keep in mind that it has been officially renamed the 'Narendra Modi Stadium'.
If a question asks about the 'Arun Jaitley Stadium', its location is New Delhi. This is simply the updated name of the historic Feroz Shah Kotla ground.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the order of the two biggest cricket stadiums in India by capacity: Na-Mo (Narendra Modi Stadium - 1st) -> Eden (Eden Gardens - 2nd).
Associate 'Lord's' (the ultimate destination or Mecca of cricket) directly with London.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions (Match the Following) pairing stadiums with their respective cities are highly common in SSC and Bank exams.
Pay special attention to recently renamed stadiums, as examiner bias heavily favors current affairs-linked static facts.
